messages:
liz (product): Need quick alignment on the "export SLA + retention-exemption" story for enterprise customers. Drafting launch criteria — wanted to surface a few tradeoffs and ask for objections.

anil (pm): TL;DR: customers want guaranteed delivery window for evidence exports (SLA), an auditable process for subpoena/hold requests, and clear behavior when BYOK prevents us from decrypting.

rohit (security): From security: two viable models: (A) customer retains exclusive key control (we cannot decrypt) and we provide encrypted blob + metadata + signed manifest; (B) optional escrow where customer grants time-limited unwrap to Redwood under strict audit/consent. Both need policy + audit.

maya (legal): Legal needs model B for court orders where customer can't/won't cooperate. Escrow must require customer opt-in and explicit contractual terms. Also need canonical wording for attestations and chain-of-custody.

clara (cs): Customers consistently ask: "how fast do we get the export?" Suggest SLA tiers: Standard (48h), Priority (8h), Emergency (24h with legal-approved escrow). Pricing TBD.

victor (sre): Operational constraints: Priority/Emergency require reserved export workers or pre-warmed nodes, and multipart/WAN-optimized transfer to customer S3. Need spec for max concurrent priority exports per region.

liz (product): Proposed acceptance tests (auto-able):
- AT1: Enqueue export (1GB) standard; confirm manifest appears and final package available within 48h.
- AT2: Enqueue export with CMEK; confirm package is encrypted and manifest contains cmk_id and key_policy_version.
- AT3: Escrow flow: customer opt-in -> escrow request with legal-proof -> escrow unwrap succeeds only after customer ACK or legal attestation; all events logged.
- AT4: Regional export routing: EU tenant export stays in EU endpoints unless explicit out-of-region consent.
- AT5: Integrity validation: manifest signature verifies and file checksums match after download.
- AT6: GC + legal hold test: create snapshot, apply legal hold, attempt GC -> operation blocked and audited.

anil (pm): Also add per-export delivery receipts: when we push to customer S3 or transfer endpoint, we need a signed receipt that includes transfer checksum, transfer time, and server-side signature.

rohit (security): Add test for key-rotation: rotate customer key; ensure old exports remain decryptable via key-rotation-metadata or we record inability in manifest with guidance. If we support rewrap-on-rotate, add tests.

maya (legal): Acceptance gating: attestation generation must be human-auditable and include principal identities (who requested, who approved), timestamps, and exact query/filter parameters. This must be producible within 24h for pilot.

victor (sre): Metric hooks we need: export_queue_depth, export_success_rate, export_median_time_by_size_bucket, multipart_retries, export_bytes_transferred. Alerts for >5% failure over 30m. Also burn-rate estimate for retention tiers (7/30/90/365).

liz (product): Quick API sketch (comments welcome):

```
POST /v1/tenants/:tid/exports
{ "range": "2025-02-01..2025-02-28", "encryption": "CMEK|PLATFORM", "cmk_arn": "arn:aws:kms:...",
  "delivery": {"type":"s3","endpoint":"s3://cust-bucket/path"}, "priority":"standard|priority|emergency",
  "escrow_opt_in": true|false
}

GET /v1/tenants/:tid/exports/:id/status  -> returns manifest_url, escrow_state, receipts
```

anil (pm): For rollout gates I'm thinking: docs + internal playbook -> pilot with two security-heavy customers -> opt-in beta (feature flag) -> GA. Each gate: all ATs green + security/legal signoff + runbook for oncall.

rohit (security): One more: escrow-state lifecycle must be auditable and immutable events stored in WORM storage for 7 years. If we can't do WORM now, document compensating control.

maya (legal): We will require customer consent UI + contract amendment for escrow. Draft required consent text and attach to PR.

clara (cs): I'll pre-notify pilot customers and collect sample SLO expectations. Also ask if they want regional delivery endpoints in their contract.

victor (sre): I need estimates: worst-case export concurrency per region, and cost delta for moving from 30-day to 365-day retention (per TB). I'll put numbers in the runbook draft.

liz (product): Action items:
- Anil: finalize SLA tier definitions + pricing input by Fri.
- Rohit: security appendix on escrow + WORM timeline + key-rotation options by Tue.
- Maya: consent text + attestation template by Tue.
- Victor: retention cost estimates + runbook skeleton by Wed.
- Clara: customer communications plan for pilots by Wed.

infra-bot: infra job scheduled: export-orchestrator v4.0 -> staging 2026-04-03T14:15:00Z

anil (pm): small open question: Should Emergency SLA require physical phone approval from legal? If yes, add to runbook.

maya (legal): For emergency escrow unwraps we require dual-approval (legal + customer ops) except court order route. We'll document exceptions.

rohit (security): locking this as draft. I'll spin up a sec-req ticket for escrow design and link it in the PR.

liz (product): Thanks everyone. I'll open PR with the acceptance tests + rollout gates in ~2hrs. Post any objections here before I merge.

clara (cs): :rocket: happy to help with pilot comms.
